scholarships.title: Petroleum Technology Development Fund (PTDF) In-Country Scholarship Scheme (ISS) 2026/27
scholarships.funding_label: Scholarship (coverage not itemised in the published guidelines)
scholarships.official_source: Petroleum Technology Development Fund (PTDF), a Federal Government of Nigeria agency

existing.description: The Petroleum Technology Development Fund is a Nigerian federal government agency mandated with developing indigenous human capacity and petroleum technology for the oil and gas industry. The Fund invites applications from qualified Nigerians for its 2026/27 Undergraduate, Master's and PhD scholarships, restricted to Nigerian public universities and to a published list of sponsored courses grouped into engineering, science, environmental science, renewable energy and management. Undergraduate applicants must already be at 200 level in a Nigerian public university and must hold a valid admission letter; MSc and PhD applicants must hold full-time admission letters and a minimum Second Class Lower (2:2) in an oil and gas-related field. Selection is merit-driven and explicitly weighted toward equitable representation of the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory.
eligibility: Be a Nigerian citizen applying to study at a Nigerian public university only
Possess a National Identity Number (NIN) and verify it before applying; NIMC verification charges apply
Not have previously held a PTDF scholarship at the same or a lower level of degree
Undergraduate: be presently at 200 level and have completed first-year examinations
Undergraduate: hold a valid admission letter into the university
Undergraduate: possess at least 5 credits in WAEC/SSCE/NECO including English Language and Mathematics
Undergraduate: hold a minimum CGPA of 2.4 on a scale of 5.0 (Second Class Lower)
Postgraduate: possess a full-time admission letter into a public university
Postgraduate: hold a minimum of Second Class Lower (2:2) in an oil and gas-related field
Postgraduate: possess a National Youth Service Corps certificate or letter of exemption
Study a course on the published list of sponsored courses
Study full time; admission for part-time studies is not considered in any category
existing.eligibility_summary: Nigerian citizens in public universities, at 200 level for undergraduate applicants, with a valid admission letter, at least five WAEC/SSCE/NECO credits including English and Mathematics, and a minimum CGPA of 2.4 of 5.0 for undergraduates or Second Class Lower for postgraduates, in a sponsored oil and gas, energy or management-related course. A National Identity Number is mandatory before applying, and all applicants must submit a certificate of indigeneship.
benefits: Scholarship award for Undergraduate, Master's or PhD study in a Nigerian public university
Access to the full published list of sponsored engineering, science, environmental science, renewable energy and management courses
coverage: Scholarship award for undergraduate, master's and doctoral study at Nigerian public universities on sponsored courses
requirements: Apply through the PTDF Scholarship Management Portal at scholarship.ptdf.gov.ng
Verify your National Identity Number before starting the application
Upload all documents as legible PDFs at the file sizes indicated in the portal
Undergraduates: upload WAEC/SSCE/NECO results, admission letter, signed and stamped first-year transcript, certificate of indigeneship and a 300-word personal statement
MSc applicants: submit a personal statement of at least 1,000 words covering reasons for the study, relevance to the industry and expected impact on national development

PhD applicants: submit a research proposal of no more than 6 pages covering topic, introduction, literature review, research questions, methodology, mode of data collection, expected outcomes, novelty, relevance to the industry and references
Postgraduates: upload first-degree certificate or statement of results, NYSC certificate or exemption letter, WAEC/SSCE/NECO results, admission letter and certificate of indigeneship
PhD applicants additionally upload a second-degree certificate or statement of results
PhD applicants: download the proposal template from the applicant's profile on the portal
Attend an oral interview if shortlisted
documents: National Identity Number with NIMC verification

WAEC/SSCE/NECO results showing at least 5 credits including English Language and Mathematics (no more than 2 sittings; for undergraduates the first sitting result must be uploaded, for postgraduates both results must precede the first degree)
Letter of admission into the university (mandatory for undergraduates)
First-year academic transcript signed and stamped by the HOD, Exams Officer or other authorised university personnel (undergraduates)
Certificate of indigeneship showing state of origin and local government
Personal statement of a minimum 300 words for undergraduates and 1,000 words for MSc applicants
First-degree certificate or statement of results (postgraduates)
NYSC certificate or letter of exemption (postgraduates)
Second-degree certificate or statement of results (PhD applicants)
PhD research proposal of no more than 6 pages using the portal template
existing.english_requirement: Not published as a test requirement. English Language is one of the five mandatory WAEC/SSCE/NECO credits required of all applicants, which is a secondary-school pass requirement rather than a language-proficiency test.
application_method: Obtain and verify a National Identity Number before applying
Read the application requirements on the PTDF Scholarship Management Portal
Access the online application form through the PTDF Scholarship Management Portal at scholarship.ptdf.gov.ng
Complete the online application form and upload all required documents as legible PDFs at the sizes indicated
Download the PhD proposal template from the applicant profile on the portal if applying to the PhD scheme
Postgraduate applicants who meet the requirements are shortlisted and invited for oral interviews before final selection
existing.selection_notes: The scholarship is described as highly competitive and merit-driven. Undergraduate final selection is based on grades on transcripts, which must be signed and stamped by the HOD, Exams Officer or other authorised university personnel. A selection panel assesses postgraduate applications on academic merit as evidenced by quality of degrees, full academic transcripts, other professional qualifications and relevant publications; membership of professional bodies; the viability of the study or research plan for PhD applicants; the statement of purpose for undergraduate and MSc applicants; and the research proposal for PhD applicants. Selection is based on equitable representation of the 36 states of the Federation and the Federal Capital Territory, except where a state does not have the requisite number of candidates to fill its allotted slots.
existing.best_fit: Nigerian public-university students at 200 level, or MSc/PhD applicants with a 2:2 or better in an oil and gas, energy or management-related discipline, pursuing one of the Fund's named sponsored courses and prepared to serve the oil and gas sector and national development.
existing.notes: The 2026/27 window closed on 5 June 2026, so this record is status upcoming/recurring rather than open, and deadline_date is null because no 2027/28 window is published. The published guidelines do not itemise what the scholarship pays for, so tuition_coverage is recorded as false and funding_amount as null rather than assumed. Part-time admission is not considered in any category, and previous PTDF scholarship holders cannot apply for the same or a lower degree category. Note also that certificate of indigeneship and a state-level quota operate together, which makes the geographic distribution of candidates a practical constraint on who can be shortlisted.
existing.duration: Not published as a fixed award term; the scheme covers Undergraduate, Master's and PhD awards within Nigerian public universities, with undergraduate eligibility anchored to study at 200 level
existing.application_period: 27 April 2026 to 5 June 2026 for the 2026/27 cycle. No 2027/28 window is published as of 2026-10-04; PTDF publishes an annual cycle under the same scheme.
existing.deadline_display: Friday 5 June 2026 (2026/27 cycle: applications opened Monday 27 April 2026 and closed Friday 5 June 2026, a six-week window)
